_comment: DBE NSC Grade 12 Geography P1, November 2024. Full-fidelity transcription:
every sub-question verbatim from the question paper (text layer read
page-by-page with pdftotext -layout, figures verified against rendered
page images), memo answers verbatim from the official Marking Guidelines.
Figures are described in [FIGURE: ...] brackets inside 'context'.
NOTE ON 2024 FORMAT: from 2024 the NSC Geography exam has no separate
mapwork paper feeding P1 topics - P1 itself is Climate & Weather (Q1),
Geomorphology (Q2) plus Section B mapwork (Q3, 1:50 000 topographical map
2829DB LADYSMITH and 1:10 000 orthophoto map 2829 DB 6 LADYSMITH).
The physical map sheets are separate and not in this repo, so map-read
inputs for calculations come from the memo's accepted values.
MEMO ANOMALY: page 3 of the marking-guidelines PDF is a marking-principles
demonstration (a sample marked script from a different paper - e.g. it
shows '1.1.1 A (South Atlantic High)'). It is NOT the answer key for this
paper; the real answers start on memo page 4 ('SECTION A').

questions.context: 1.4 Refer to the infographic below based on Tropical Cyclone Filipo. TROPICAL CYCLONE FILIPO: 'The tropical storm made landfall in Mozambique on 12 March after strengthening off the coast of southeast Africa, bringing strong winds and heavy rain to Mozambique. On 13 March, Tropical Storm Filipo moved back over the ocean and developed into a tropical cyclone on 14 March.' [FIGURE: Map (South African Weather Services) of south-east Africa showing the plotted path of TC Filipo: from 10 Mar 12:00 UTC over the Indian Ocean it tracks west/south-west (positions 11 Mar 12:00, 11 Mar 18:00, 12 Mar 6:00 UTC) crossing the Mozambique coast, passes near Maputo (13 Mar 6:00 UTC), then curves back south-east over the Indian Ocean (13 Mar 18:00, 14 Mar 6:00 UTC). Inset synoptic sketch labelled MATURE STAGE showing closed isobars (984 and 980 hPa) spiralling around the eye.] TABLE - INFORMATION ON THE PATH OF TROPICAL CYCLONE FILIPO (DATE, TIME, WIND): 10 Mar 12:00 UTC 63 km/h; 11 Mar 12:00 UTC 95 km/h; 11 Mar 18:00 UTC 116 km/h; 12 Mar 06:00 UTC 95 km/h; 12 Mar 18:00 UTC 74 km/h; 13 Mar 06:00 UTC 84 km/h; 13 Mar 18:00 UTC 106 km/h; 14 Mar 06.00 UTC 127 km/h.

questions.context: 2.5 Refer to the extract below on catchment and river management. MANAGEMENT OF CATCHMENT AREAS AND RIVER NETWORKS (SYSTEMS): 'River catchments are under severe pressure in some parts of South Africa. The plentiful water they provide has meant that the fertile ground surrounding them is an ideal place for agricultural activities. They are areas of natural beauty and often support both plant and animal species. Unfortunately, humans have not always recognised the importance of river catchments. When toxins and heavy metals leach into the catchment areas, they can endanger the lives of the flora and fauna. Agricultural run-off can carry chemicals into river catchments, creating an imbalance in nutrient levels and impacts on different species in different ways. Fortunately, we are now beginning to pay attention to the conservation of these vital natural resources.' [Adapted from https://www.envirotech-online.com/news/water-wastewater/9/breaking-news/what-is-classed-as-a-river-58892]

questions.memo_working: Length: 3,0 cm x 0,1 = 0,30 (1) km. Breadth: 2,2 (1) cm [accepted measurement range 2,1 cm - 2,3 cm] x 0,1 = 0,22 (1) km [range 0,21 km - 0,23 km]. Area = 0,30 km x 0,22 km = 0,066 (0,07) km² (1) [range 0,06 - 0,07 km²]. (On the 1:10 000 orthophoto map 1 cm = 0,1 km; breadth is measured off the map by the candidate.)
questions.map_reference: Demarcated feature 6 in blocks A4/A5 and block B4 on orthophoto map 2829 DB 6 LADYSMITH

questions.text: Give a reason why the expansion of the demarcated feature 6 (answer to QUESTION 3.1.5) is limited in a south-easterly direction? (1 x 1)
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: Map skills and calculations
questions.memo_answer: Due to the river (1); Row of trees forms a buffer zone (1); There is a recreational area (accept greenbelt) (1) [ANY ONE]

questions.context: 3.2 MAP INTERPRETATION. Refer to F in block C2 and G in block D4 on the topographical map.
questions.text: (a) The temperature at F in the centre of the town is 2 °C higher than at G. Name the concept that describes this difference. (1 x 1)
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: Map interpretation (urban climate)
questions.map_reference: F in block C2; G in block D4 (topographical map)

questions.text: (b) Give ONE reason why the high density of buildings at F generally contributes to the higher temperatures. (1 x 2)
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: Map interpretation (urban climate)
questions.memo_answer: Heat will get trapped (2); Reduced wind speed (2); Reduced air flow (2); Artificial surfaces (2); Multiple reflections (2) [ANY ONE]

questions.context: Refer to blocks D2 and D3 on the orthophoto map.
questions.text: Explain how aspect of slope determined the location of Rose Park at 7 on the orthophoto map. (1 x 2)
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: Map interpretation (aspect and settlement)
questions.memo_answer: Rose Park at 7 is located on the north (east)-facing slope which is warmer / receives more insolation (2). [PART MARKING: Rose Park at 7 is located on the north (east)-facing slope (1); MAXIMUM 1 MARK]

questions.context: Refer to the dam H in block B1 on the topographical map.
questions.text: The dam wall indicates that the river is flowing in a … direction.  A south-westerly  B north-easterly  C north-westerly  D south-easterly (1 x 1)
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: Map interpretation (drainage)
questions.memo_note: Memo accepts both A (south-westerly) and D (south-easterly).
questions.map_reference: Dam H in block B1 (topographical map)

questions.context: Refer to the weir at I in block A3 on the topographical map.
questions.text: A weir is used to regulate (control) the flow of water in a river. Explain why the construction of the weir was necessary. (1 x 2)
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: Map interpretation (river management)
questions.memo_answer: To reduce the risk of flooding due to the confluence of rivers (2); To reduce the risk of flooding downstream (cultivated land, built-up area, railway line, caravan park) (2) [ANY ONE]. [PART MARKING: To reduce the risk of flooding (1); MAXIMUM 1 MARK]
questions.map_reference: Weir at I in block A3 (topographical map)

questions.context: Refer to the section of the Klip River from 8 in block A2 to 9 in block A5 on the orthophoto map.
questions.text: Identify the fluvial landform/feature. (1 x 1)
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: Map interpretation (fluvial landforms)
questions.map_reference: Klip River from 8 in block A2 to 9 in block A5 (orthophoto map)

questions.text: Give evidence why this fluvial landform/feature (answer to QUESTION 3.2.5) developed in this area. (1 x 1)
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: Map interpretation (fluvial landforms)
questions.memo_answer: Land is flat/gentle (accept lower course) (1); Contour lines are far apart (1) [ANY ONE]

questions.context: Refer to block C5 on the orthophoto map.
questions.text: Why will more erosion take place at 11 than at 10? (1 x 2)
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: Map interpretation (fluvial processes)
questions.memo_answer: Water flows faster on the outer bank /11/ undercut slope (2); Water flows slower on the inner bank /10/ slip-off slope (2) [ANY ONE]

questions.context: 3.3 GEOGRAPHICAL INFORMATION SYSTEMS (GIS).
questions.text: The vertical aerial photograph used to make the orthophoto map has a (high/low) resolution. (1 x 1)
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: GIS

questions.text: The reference of the topographical map represents (spatial/attribute) data. (1 x 1)
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: GIS

questions.text: How does this data (answer to QUESTION 3.3.2) assist in identifying feature J on the topographical map? (1 x 2)
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: GIS
questions.memo_answer: It indicates what feature J represents in reality (2); The reference shows that the symbol at J is an excavation (2); To distinguish between similar land-use features (mine dump and mine excavation) (2) [ANY ONE]

questions.context: Refer to 12 in block C2 on the orthophoto map.
questions.text: Define the term buffering. (1 x 2)
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: GIS
questions.memo_answer: The demarcation of an area around/along a geographical feature/location (2) [CONCEPT]

questions.text: How would buffering at 12 protect the quality of the water in the Klip River? (1 x 2)
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: GIS
questions.memo_answer: Restrict development on the banks of the river (2); Decrease pollution from the built-up area (2); Reduces eroded soil from entering the river (2); Decreased eutrophication (2); Reduces salinity (2); The natural course/capacity of the river will be maintained (2); Biodiversity of the river will be preserved (2) [ANY ONE]
